reason: The quality is wrinkling. 'Reticulately' only says the wrinkles form a network; if that detail is wanted it can be added as a second value, reticulate (FLOPO:0991100), with no new term.
A hyphenated compound of two existing shape values, handled like 'linear-lanceolate' as a continuum between the two values.
A testa with ladder-like transverse ribs is exactly what scalariform means; 'ribbed' only says what the rungs are made of.
A root-stock is a part, not a quality; PO lists 'rootstock' as a synonym of rhizome.

A 'rose flush' is a pink tinge on the part, so the quality is the colour pink. PATO_0002518 'flush' means level with a surface and must not be used. 'On fading' is a stage, and 'on keel' is a region of the part.
Lenticular already maps to biconvex (previous rule C202); a lens is round in outline anyway, so 'round' adds nothing.
A compound of two existing outline shapes, handled as a continuum between them.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum: spherical PATO_0001499 + ovate PATO_0001891, synonym ovoid)
reason: A compound of two existing solid shapes, handled as a continuum between them. When pato#627 is merged, the ovoid value should move to the new PATO ovoid term.
Scapeless means without a scape; the previous review maps scape to peduncle (rule C255). The French 'subscapeuse' example is a different word (nearly scapose) and should not use this rule.
A degree adverb ('scarcely revolute', 'scarcely prominent'), not a quality. The degree belongs to the statement record together with the quality it modifies.
'Fruit schizocarpic' says the fruit is a schizocarp, which is a PO fruit type, not a quality.
'Semi-' weakens an existing value in the same way as 'sub-' in 'suborbicular', so it is an approximate value of inflexible (synonym stiff).

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum: serrulate FLOPO:0991081 + scalloped PATO_0001889, synonym crenate)
reason: A compound of two existing margin values, handled as a continuum between them.

A margin fringed with minute bristles. The diminutive maps to the existing value, as strigillose did to strigulose, and the margin is already the bearer. PATO_0001408 'ciliated' is about cells and must not be used.

This describes chemical make-up (contains silica), not a shape or texture quality. Both examples are fragments ('a high proportion…'). If needed, it is better stated as silica present than as a FLOPO value.
Soboliferous means producing soboles, i.e. suckers from the base or below ground; PO lists 'sucker' as a synonym here. Soboles can also come from rhizomes, so the PO match is approximate.

label: sour-tasting
definition: A flavourful quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's having a sharp, acid flavour. NOTE: Sibling of PATO:0002474 bitter; different from FLOPO:0991019 sour-smelling, which is an odour.
reason: A real taste quality of sap and fruit flesh. PATO has bitter but no sour, and its old taste terms are obsolete.
A compound of two existing outline shapes, handled as a continuum between them.

target: new: colour of markings (spotted PATO_0000333 + green PATO_0000320 of the spots)
reason: Two existing values: the part is spotted, and the spots are green. The green belongs to the spots, not the whole part, so it needs a 'markings' slot rather than a new term.
A manner adverb on a growth or branching habit ('stiffly branched', 'stiffly ascending'), not a quality of the part.
Rhizomatous means a rhizome is present. 'Stout' is a quality of the rhizome and belongs in a separate statement about it.
A compound of two hair types, each mapping to an existing value (the diminutives map to the base value), handled as a continuum.
Nearly equal in length, either among like parts or 'to' another part. This is an approximate equality, covered by the existing patterns.
'Sub-' plus an existing value, handled as an approximate value like 'suborbicular'.

label: trullate
definition: A 2-D shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's outline being shaped like a trowel blade: angular, with straight sides, broadest below the middle. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991024 ovate (curved sides) and PATO:0001938 rhomboid (broadest at the middle).
reason: Trullate is a standard botanical outline term with no PATO or FLOPO class. 'Sub-' is then handled by the approximate-value pattern. Only two statements, so its priority is low.
'Suffused with purple' means tinged purple all over, so the quality is the colour purple. 'Evidently not' is a negation that goes in the statement record.
The two uses mean different things (tiered horizontal branching vs. the French 'tronc tabulé', probably about buttresses). Two statements are not enough to pin down either meaning.
A fragment left by a shared hyphen ('thin- to thick-walled'). The full word belongs to the continuum statement it was cut from.
A generic part: it needs the organ it belongs to, as with 'lobe' and 'beak' in the previous review.
Vague comparison ('trunk-like branches' means branches as stout as a trunk). 'Distinct trunk' is just the bearer stem (PO_0009047, synonym trunk).
